h1: Steel Roof Trusses in Pakistan: Light, Strong Members for Long Spans
quickAnswer: A truss is a frame of straight members arranged in triangles, so it spans long distances with little steel. Steel Mind Engineers fabricates pitched, parallel-chord and space trusses for roofs and sheds.
alt: Steel truss roof of an open industrial shed in Pakistan.

faq.q: Is a truss cheaper than a solid beam?
faq.a: For long spans, often yes. A truss uses less steel for the same span.

faq.q: How long can a truss be?
faq.a: It depends on the load and the depth. The engineer will advise.

blocks.text: A truss is a frame made of straight members arranged in triangles. The triangles share the load, so each member carries only tension or compression. This lets a truss span a long distance with little steel.
Trusses support the roofs of sheds, workshops, halls, stadium stands, petrol stations and farms. They suit open-sided buildings, where their shape is also visible and attractive.

A pitched truss has a top chord that slopes to both sides, the usual shape for sheds. A parallel-chord truss has parallel top and bottom chords and suits flat roofs and floor systems. A space truss is a three-dimensional frame for very large roofs.

Trusses can use steel tubes or angle sections. Tubes look clean and resist weather well. Angles are easy to connect and often cost less. The engineer will recommend one based on span, load and budget.
Long trusses are made in parts, delivered on trucks and joined on site. Steel Mind Engineers plans the splice points so that each part can travel and be lifted safely.
